inventory.acceptance: On level ground, increasing speed increases estimated power; at 30 km/h, 85 kg, Crr 0.004, CdA 0.32 m², air density 1.225 kg/m³ and 97% drivetrain efficiency, rider power is about 145.5 W.
inventory.boundary: Steady-speed physics estimate only, not a power-meter reading, training prescription, race predictor or bike-fit recommendation. It assumes a straight road and constant conditions; does not model drafting, acceleration, surface variation, gusts or elevation profiles. Negative downhill demand is clamped to zero; braking and regenerative power are not modeled. Calculation remains in the browser.

functions: estimate single-layer air-core solenoid inductance from coil diameter, winding length and turns using Wheeler’s approximation
calculate toroid inductance from the exact core manufacturer AL factor and turns
estimate whole turns required for a user-entered inductance target
show the method and its practical limits without assuming a generic magnetic material
inventory.acceptance: For an air-core single-layer coil with 10 turns, 20 mm diameter and 20 mm winding length, Wheeler gives about 1.36 µH. Doubling turns quadruples inductance. A toroid with AL=100 nH/turn² and 10 turns gives 10 µH and needs 10 turns for a 10 µH target.
inventory.boundary: Browser-only estimate, not a measurement or SPICE simulation. The air-core mode uses Wheeler’s single-layer approximation; the toroid mode requires AL from the exact core datasheet. Does not model wire thickness, winding spacing, core saturation/loss, temperature, frequency, parasitic capacitance, current, safety or tolerance. Verify a real design against manufacturer data and measurement.

functions: calculate inward acceleration and force from mass, radius and linear speed
derive linear speed from radius and rotation frequency in hertz or rpm
convert the result to RPM, angular velocity, period and customary force units
show the speed-squared relationship and distinguish the ideal model from real engineering design
inventory.acceptance: For a 2 kg mass moving at 4 m/s around a 0.5 m radius, acceleration is 32 m/s² and centripetal force is 64 N. Doubling speed quadruples both acceleration and force. A 2 Hz rotation at 0.5 m radius gives 2π m/s and 16π² N for a 2 kg mass.
inventory.boundary: Ideal Newtonian uniform circular-motion calculation only. Does not model tangential acceleration, varying radius, gravity, friction, structural stress, vehicle handling, relativistic speeds, or certify safety. No uploaded data, account, server processing or API.

functions: create separate writing projects with optional word-count goals
record dated writing sessions with words, minutes and an optional note
edit or delete a session by stable ID so updates never double-count words
review project totals, goal progress, writing days and current-day streak
save the log only in browser storage and export a spreadsheet-safe CSV backup
inventory.acceptance: A project with a 1,000-word goal and sessions of 400 then 250 words shows 650 words and 65% progress. Editing the second session to 300 words changes the total to 700, not 950.
inventory.boundary: A manual session log, not an automatic document word counter, writing-quality evaluator, cloud backup or synchronized account. Browser storage can be cleared or unavailable; users should export a CSV if they want an independent backup. CSV text cells are protected against spreadsheet formula injection. No session data is uploaded or sent to a server.

functions: encrypt or decrypt UTF-8 text locally with AES-256-GCM and authenticated decryption
encrypt or decrypt bounded files in a versioned binary container with random salt and nonce
derive a key from a long passphrase with PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA-256 at a fixed documented iteration count
reject unsupported or altered containers and return no plaintext when authentication fails
avoid sending or saving the passphrase, plaintext, ciphertext or files to a server
inventory.acceptance: Text and binary-file round trips reproduce the original bytes. A wrong passphrase or one-bit ciphertext change fails authentication and returns no plaintext.
inventory.boundary: Browser Web Crypto encryption utility, not a cryptographic audit, password manager, secure-delete tool or guarantee against malware, compromised devices, weak passphrases or browser extensions. Uses AES-256-GCM with a fresh random 96-bit nonce and 128-bit tag, and PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA-256 with 600,000 iterations and a fresh 128-bit salt. Encrypted outputs are portable containers; losing the passphrase means the data cannot be recovered. File mode is capped at 16 MiB to bound browser memory use. Keep backups and verify the recipient can decrypt before relying on the data.

functions: create a compact HS256 JWT from a JSON claims object and a locally entered secret
optionally add an exp NumericDate from a user-selected duration of up to 365 days
verify an HS256 signature locally and separately report exp/nbf timing without treating it as user authentication
reject malformed JSON, unsupported algorithms, altered tokens and oversized inputs
never upload or persist claims, tokens or secrets
inventory.acceptance: A token built from a JSON object verifies locally with its original secret; changing one claim or using another secret fails; an optional 60-second expiration is active at second 1,059 and expired at second 1,060 when issued at second 1,000.
inventory.boundary: Local HS256 signing/signature verification utility, not an identity provider, authentication service, authorization decision, key vault or production token-management system. Signature verification does not establish who issued a token or whether its claims are trusted; check issuer, audience, keys, clock and application policy independently. Secrets and tokens stay in this browser tab and are not saved or sent to a server. Enforces the RFC 7518 minimum of a 256-bit HS256 key and a 64 KiB JSON / 128 KiB token limit.

functions: calculate gross yield from annual rent and purchase price
estimate effective rent after an entered vacancy percentage
subtract annual property tax, maintenance, insurance, association fees and other expenses to estimate net operating income and net yield
show a monthly average and clearly separate gross rent from net income
inventory.acceptance: Monthly rent 1,000 and purchase price 200,000 returns 12,000 gross annual rent and 6% gross yield. With 5% vacancy and 3,600 annual expenses, net operating income is 7,800 and net yield is 3.9%.
inventory.boundary: A simple rental-property operating-yield estimate, not a valuation, investment recommendation, tax calculation or financing model. Excludes mortgage/debt service, closing costs, income taxes, depreciation, capital gains and future rent/price changes. Expense categories are user-entered and do not establish a complete budget.

secondaryIntents: encrypt short text with RSA public key
functions: generate extractable RSA-OAEP key pairs at 2048 or 3072 bits with SHA-256 in browser Web Crypto
export public SPKI and private PKCS8 keys as PEM and show a SHA-256 fingerprint of the public DER key
encrypt and decrypt short UTF-8 messages locally using the selected public/private key
enforce OAEP plaintext byte limits of 190 bytes at 2048 bits and 318 bytes at 3072 bits
reject certificates, PKCS#1 PEM, oversized or malformed keys and ciphertext
inventory.acceptance: A generated key pair round-trips a short message; the wrong private key and a changed ciphertext fail; 190 UTF-8 bytes succeed with RSA-2048/SHA-256 and 191 bytes are rejected.
inventory.boundary: Local Web Crypto demonstration, not a trusted identity, certificate authority, audited key-management system or security guarantee. RSA-OAEP/SHA-256 only encrypts short messages; use an audited hybrid-encryption protocol for larger data. Private keys are displayed/exportable and are not uploaded or backed up; losing or exposing one can permanently disclose data. No private key is stored by the page.

secondaryIntents: analyze HTTP status codes from logs
functions: parse only Apache/Nginx combined access-log lines with explicit format validation
report valid, invalid and unsupported non-empty line counts plus up to 20 invalid line numbers without echoing source text
aggregate request counts by HTTP status, method and UTC date, and reported response bytes
filter aggregates by 2xx–5xx status class and inclusive UTC date range
export only aggregate status/date counts to CSV without IPs, paths, query strings, user agents or referrers
inventory.acceptance: A log with three supported entries and one invalid line reports three parsed and one invalid; status/method/day totals match, date offsets convert to UTC, and the exported CSV contains no original IP, path, query, referrer, user-agent or invalid-line content.
inventory.boundary: Privacy-focused summary for Apache/Nginx combined access logs only; not a security audit, anomaly detector, latency profiler or complete log platform. Unsupported formats count as invalid, not guessed. Processing stays in this browser; raw lines are not returned in the analysis and are not uploaded or stored. Caps: 10 MiB, 100,000 lines and 8,192 characters per line. The aggregate CSV includes status and date counts only.

secondaryIntents: customer acquisition cost and payback calculator
functions: sum marketing, sales, tools, agency and other acquisition expenses for a single period
calculate blended CAC from total acquisition spend and newly acquired customers
estimate gross-profit payback using monthly revenue per customer and entered gross margin
accept a user-selected supported ISO currency code without converting exchange rates
run locally and clearly distinguish an average CAC from channel attribution or customer lifetime value
inventory.acceptance: 1000 in same-period acquisition spend and 10 new customers returns CAC 100; at 50 monthly revenue per customer and 80% margin estimated gross-profit payback is 2.5 months.
inventory.boundary: Blended arithmetic estimate, not marginal/channel CAC, campaign attribution, customer lifetime value, accounting or financial advice. Spend and acquired customers must use the same period and scope. Payback excludes churn, payment timing, taxes, overhead and cohort variation. No exchange-rate conversion, upload, storage or server processing.

functions: estimate room cooling capacity from floor dimensions and ceiling height using the published ENERGY STAR room-air-conditioner bands
adjust the estimate with explicit user-selected insulation, sunlight, extra occupants and kitchen factors
show the base value, each adjustment, room area and approximate volume so assumptions are visible
handle zero floor area as zero load and flag dimensions outside the reference chart instead of extrapolating a false precision
inventory.acceptance: A 12 × 12 ft room with an 8 ft ceiling, typical insulation, typical sun, two occupants and no kitchen returns 5,000 Btu/h; zero floor area returns zero, never a negative load.
inventory.boundary: A room-air-conditioner planning estimate based on ENERGY STAR size bands and its published sunlight, occupant and kitchen adjustments; insulation and ceiling height are transparent user assumptions. It is not a Manual J load calculation, central HVAC design, energy audit or equipment recommendation. Actual loads depend on climate, envelope, windows, infiltration, orientation and other conditions. Check manufacturer guidance and consult a qualified HVAC professional; local-only arithmetic, no uploaded measurements.

secondaryIntents: how many solar panels do I need
functions: estimate daily, monthly and yearly output from panel count or estimate the panel count for a manually entered daily energy target
apply user-entered peak sun hours and system loss percentage
estimate panel area when both panel dimensions are supplied
estimate annual bill offset from a manually entered energy tariff and simple payback from a manually entered installed cost
inventory.acceptance: A 1 kW array with 5 peak sun hours produces 5 kWh/day before losses; at 20% entered losses it estimates 4 kWh/day, 121.67 kWh/month and 1,460 kWh/year.
inventory.boundary: Illustrative estimate only. Peak sun hours, losses, panel rating and dimensions are user supplied; real output varies with location, season, shading, orientation, temperature, inverter and system condition. Savings assume every generated kWh offsets a purchased kWh at the entered tariff; actual self-consumption, export credits, utility fees, incentives, degradation, financing and maintenance are not modeled. Not electrical, installation or financial advice; consult a qualified solar professional. Runs locally and retains no inputs.

functions: estimate pavers from a rectangular surface and a repeat module with one or more pieces
count complete modules in the entered orientation and apply optional extra pavers
calculate the edge perimeter for edging materials
estimate an optional base layer volume, allowance and user-entered material cost
inventory.acceptance: A 10 m × 10 m surface using a 40 cm × 40 cm repeat module with one paver per module needs 625 full modules/pavers; a 10 cm base layer is 10 m³ and the edge perimeter is 40 m.
inventory.boundary: Planning estimate only: counts complete repeating modules in the entered orientation and does not create a cut or layout plan. Edge cuts may produce reusable offcuts. It does not assess drainage, soil, loading, frost depth or construction-code requirements; follow product instructions and consult a qualified installer. Inputs stay in this browser.

functions: load a local raster image
sample exact source pixels by pointer or keyboard with optional zoom
show source coordinates, HEX, RGB and alpha
build, copy and remove colors from a local palette
inventory.acceptance: Sampling a fully opaque pure-red source pixel returns RGB 255, 0, 0 and HEX #FF0000 at its exact source coordinates; transparent pixels retain their alpha value.
inventory.boundary: Samples colors from a local image; it does not convert a typed color or identify a named color. Image decoding and preview use this device. Limited to 12 megapixels to keep memory use bounded; no image is uploaded.

functions: load a local raster image
select multiple regions by pointer or exact pixel coordinates
pixelate, blur or permanently cover each selected region with black
preview edits and export a fresh PNG or JPEG locally
inventory.acceptance: A black-redacted region exports only black pixels in that region; source image remains unchanged and is never uploaded.
inventory.boundary: Local image-region redaction, not a global mosaic or general photo editor. Blur and pixelation may leave details inferable; use opaque black for sensitive data. Processing depends on browser/device memory and is limited to 24 megapixels.

functions: load a local raster image
adjust unsharp-mask radius, amount and threshold with a before/after comparison
preview at reduced dimensions and export a sharpened PNG or JPEG at the original dimensions
inventory.acceptance: An amount of zero leaves every decoded RGBA pixel unchanged in the processing pipeline; PNG output preserves those pixel values, while JPEG export is lossy by design. Positive sharpening changes RGB edge contrast without changing dimensions or alpha.
inventory.boundary: Local edge-contrast adjustment, not AI detail recovery, denoising or the general image editor. Excessive sharpening can create halos and amplify noise; results depend on source quality and device memory. Limited to 8 megapixels.

functions: split a local raster image into an even grid or fixed pixel-size PNG tiles
add optional overlapping edge pixels for print or editing workflows
download one ZIP with the tiles and a coordinate manifest whose core rectangles reconstruct the source without gaps
inventory.acceptance: A 13 × 7 source split into a 4 × 3 grid or 5 × 3-pixel tiles has core rectangles that cover every original pixel exactly once; overlap changes crop bounds but not the gap-free core map.
inventory.boundary: Grid/tile splitting and packaging, not single-region cropping or collage composition. Browser-local, 12-megapixel and 100-tile limits protect device memory; a desktop is recommended for large jobs. Animated sources use the first frame; output is PNG. The original file is never modified or uploaded.

functions: choose a local raster image
run a pinned lightweight 2× super-resolution model in a dedicated browser worker
process bounded overlapping tiles with progress and hard cancellation
compare the enlarged preview and download a new PNG
inventory.acceptance: A supported 64 × 64 image produces a 128 × 128 output; cancelling terminates inference and never replaces the source file.
inventory.boundary: A lightweight 2× detail-reconstruction model, not a promise to recover the original scene or improve every image. Processing is limited to 1 megapixel and uses CPU, RAM and a one-time local model/runtime download of about 20 MB; desktop/laptop recommended. Transparency is composited on white. No image is uploaded.

functions: estimate wallpaper strips from wall perimeter, height and roll width
round each drop up to the pattern repeat and include a fixed trim allowance
estimate usable drops per roll and whole roll count
deduct user-entered door and window area proportionally and apply extra material
inventory.acceptance: For a 12 m perimeter, 2.4 m height, 0.53 m wide × 10.05 m roll and no waste: no pattern repeat needs 6 rolls; a 0.32 m repeat increases the estimate to 8 rolls.
inventory.boundary: Planning estimate only. It converts opening area into equivalent full-height strip width and assumes a continuous perimeter; it cannot lay out individual walls, corners, obstacles, pattern phase, damaged sections or product-specific trim. Verify roll coverage and pattern instructions on the product label and buy a practical allowance.

functions: calculate rectangle or circle planting-bed area and combine repeated beds
estimate loose mulch volume from bed area and depth
add a configurable material allowance and convert to cubic metres/yards
round up bags from a selected litre or cubic-foot bag size and optionally estimate cost
inventory.acceptance: A 5 m × 4 m bed at 5 cm depth requires 1 m³ before waste; with 50 L bags that is 20 bags. A 0% waste setting preserves the exact volume.
inventory.boundary: Material estimate only: real bed boundaries, uneven ground, settling, product coverage and package fill can change actual needs. It does not recommend plant-specific mulch depth; follow local horticultural guidance and the product label. All values stay in this browser.

functions: convert pool volume from litres or US/imperial gallons
calculate salt mass from measured current and manufacturer-specified target salinity
adjust for user-entered salt purity
estimate whole salt bags from package weight in kilograms or pounds
inventory.acceptance: For 1,000 litres and a 1,000 ppm increase, the ideal 100%-pure salt estimate is 1 kg before package rounding.
inventory.boundary: Dosage estimate only. It does not recommend a target salinity, test water or account for actual pool capacity, salt already dissolved, water exchange or product composition. Use the chlorinator manufacturer instructions, a reliable water test and chemical safety directions; never treat this estimate as a substitute.

functions: estimate posts for straight fence sections and evenly distributed gate openings
compare panel and picket infill quantities
estimate picket spacing under a user-entered maximum gap
apply extra-material allowance and optional item costs
inventory.acceptance: A 100 ft straight run with one 4 ft gate, 8 ft maximum post spacing, 8 ft panels, 5.5 in pickets, 2 in maximum gap and 10% extra estimates 14 posts, 12 panels (14 to order) and 156 pickets (172 to order); one isolated section with no gates always includes both end posts.
inventory.boundary: Planning estimate only. Gate placement is assumed even; panel and picket quantities are alternatives. It does not design shared corner posts, rails, foundations, slopes, wind resistance, hinges, latches, permits or local code compliance. Verify the layout and product dimensions with a qualified installer.

functions: calculate a uniform clear gap from an opening width, baluster thickness and chosen count
estimate the minimum baluster count that stays within a user-entered maximum gap
show total baluster width, number of clear gaps and exact uniform spacing in metric or imperial units
inventory.acceptance: For a 1,200 mm clear opening, 40 mm balusters and a 100 mm maximum gap, the minimum count is 8 and all 9 gaps are about 97.78 mm; 7 balusters would leave 115 mm gaps. Gaps plus baluster widths equal the opening width.
inventory.boundary: Layout arithmetic only. It does not determine code-compliant guard openings, strength, loads, fasteners, post details, material suitability or safety. Confirm applicable local requirements and have a qualified professional review the design before building.

functions: estimate block courses and whole blocks from a straight wall, editable block modules and joint thickness
estimate a rectangular user-dimensioned base-material volume and a rectangular backfill zone
apply a user-entered material allowance and show metric or cubic-foot quantities
inventory.acceptance: A zero-height wall returns zero block courses, blocks, base volume and backfill volume; a nonzero wall estimates whole courses and blocks by rounded-up module coverage.
inventory.boundary: Material planning estimate only. It does not design or assess wall stability, drainage, reinforcement, geogrid, foundations, soil pressure, slopes, surcharges, loads, permits or local code. The rectangular base and backfill quantities use dimensions entered by the user, not recommended design values. Have a qualified professional review retaining-wall design and follow local requirements.

functions: estimate runtime from a battery energy rating in Wh/kWh or from Ah and voltage
apply user-entered depth-of-discharge and system-efficiency percentages
show nominal and usable energy alongside hours and days for transparent assumptions
inventory.acceptance: A 100 Wh battery supplying a constant 10 W load at 100% depth of discharge and efficiency estimates 10 hours; applying 80% discharge and 90% efficiency estimates 7.2 hours.
inventory.boundary: Idealized energy arithmetic only. Runtime varies with load profile, voltage sag, temperature, battery age, chemistry, discharge rate, inverter losses and cutoff behavior. The entered efficiency and discharge percentages are assumptions, not measured performance. It does not size wiring, protection, chargers or battery systems; follow manufacturer instructions and consult a qualified electrician for installations.

functions: allocate a bounded list of linear cuts across stock boards with a selected saw kerf
show per-board cut layouts, remaining offcut and total kerf allowance
accept a single shared measurement unit and quantity per cut size
inventory.acceptance: With 2400 mm stock, 3 mm kerf and cuts 1200 × 1, 800 × 1 and 390 × 1, one board fits exactly within the 2400 mm stock after kerf; a 1200 mm piece with a 1200 mm stock and positive kerf is rejected as overlength.
inventory.boundary: A deterministic best-fit-decreasing heuristic, not a proof of globally minimal stock use. Assumes straight 1D cuts, one kerf allowance per produced piece and one shared unit; it does not model grain, defects, blade entry, clamps, trim ends, angled cuts, joinery or structural suitability. Verify every cut against real stock and tool setup before cutting.

functions: estimate plant and row counts inside a rectangular bed from center-based edge margins
compare regular grid and staggered triangular layouts
show actual layout count, planting area and approximate density in a shared length unit
inventory.acceptance: For a 5 m × 3 m bed with 0.5 m in-row and row spacing, the centered rectangular grid has 10 plants per row, 6 rows and 60 plants; increasing both spacings to 1 m reduces the count to 15. The staggered triangular mode offsets alternate rows by half the in-row spacing.
inventory.boundary: Geometric layout estimate only. Assumes a flat rectangle, uniform center spacing and a half-spacing border; it does not recommend species spacing, account for paths, irregular beds, mature canopy, roots, slope, irrigation or plant-health requirements. Follow the selected variety guidance and verify a real planting layout.

functions: estimate battery energy between user-entered starting and target state of charge
estimate grid energy and charging time from charger power and user-entered efficiency
optionally estimate electricity cost from a user-entered tariff and currency code
inventory.acceptance: For a 50 kWh battery charged from 20% to 80%, 30 kWh reaches the battery; at 90% efficiency the grid supplies about 33.333 kWh. With a constant 7.2 kW charger input, estimated time is about 4.6296 hours before real-world charging taper.
inventory.boundary: Idealized constant-power estimate. Real EVs commonly reduce power as charge rises, and vehicle limits, temperature, shared circuits, charger behavior, battery conditioning and tariff rules affect results. It does not predict a vehicle-specific charging curve, savings, charger compatibility or installation safety. Use vehicle/charger documentation and a qualified electrician for electrical work.

functions: convert a twelve-month rainfall series and roof catchment area into runoff-adjusted collection estimates
model tank storage, monthly demand, overflow and unmet demand across the year
allow metric or imperial catchment and tank-volume units with user-selected runoff efficiency
inventory.acceptance: An idealized 10 mm of rain over a 100 m² catchment at 100% runoff yields 1,000 L before tank limits or demand. Monthly storage never exceeds the chosen tank capacity and carries from one month to the next.
inventory.boundary: Planning estimate only. Uses user-entered monthly rainfall, a rectangular horizontal catchment, one runoff coefficient and a month-level sequence that adds captured rain before serving demand; actual timing, roof material, first-flush diversion, evaporation, leaks, water quality and local collection rules are not modeled. Do not assume harvested water is potable; follow local requirements and appropriate treatment guidance.

functions: calculate horizontal run and sloped surface length from a rise and user-selected slope ratio
include a user-entered count and depth for level landings in total horizontal planning length
show slope percentage and angle without selecting a legal or accessible slope
inventory.acceptance: A 1 m rise at a chosen 1:12 ratio needs 12 m of horizontal ramp run; sloped surface is sqrt(1² + 12²) m before landings.
inventory.boundary: Geometry only, not an accessibility assessment, building-code interpretation or structural design. Slope rules and required landings depend on jurisdiction, use, occupancy, rise, site and applicable standards; user-entered ratio is not validated for compliance. Have a qualified professional review plans and local requirements before construction.

functions: estimate transmission heat loss separately for walls, roof, windows and floor from entered areas and U-values
add a simplified ventilation term from room volume and air changes per hour
convert temperature difference from K or °F and report total heat-loss rate in W and BTU/h
inventory.acceptance: A component with U = 1 W/(m²·K), area 10 m² and temperature difference 20 K contributes 200 W. Total equals the sum of component and ventilation terms.
inventory.boundary: Simplified steady-state heat-loss estimate, not a heating-system sizing or energy-bill prediction. U-values and air changes are user inputs; thermal bridges, solar gains, internal gains, moisture, wind, intermittent operation, duct losses, local climate and building standards are not fully modeled. Verify assumptions with an energy professional before making building or equipment decisions.

functions: convert a user-entered heat-output rate from kW or BTU/h
estimate electrical input power and daily energy from a user-entered COP and operating hours
estimate hourly, daily and 30-day running cost from a user-entered electricity price and currency
compare energy use and cost against an idealized electric-resistance baseline delivering the same heat output

inventory.boundary: Illustrative steady-rate arithmetic only. COP, heat-output rate, operating hours, tariff and currency are user inputs; COP varies with outdoor temperature, flow temperature, system design, cycling, defrost, installation and maintenance. The resistance comparison assumes COP 1 and the same delivered heat; it is not a measured appliance comparison. No seasonal performance, climate, tariffs, taxes, fixed charges, equipment sizing or purchase advice is modeled. Verify manufacturer data, utility tariffs and local conditions; this tool runs locally and does not upload inputs.

functions: calculate linear, area, or volume change from an entered initial dimension, matching expansion coefficient, and temperature difference
convert Celsius/Fahrenheit temperature differences and coefficients per Celsius/per Fahrenheit consistently
accept common metric and imperial length, area, or volume units and report results in the selected input unit
allow negative expansion coefficients and reject combinations that imply a negative final dimension
inventory.acceptance: A 10 m bar with coefficient 12 × 10⁻⁶ per °C and a +50 °C change expands by 0.006 m to 10.006 m; a zero temperature change preserves the original length.

The user supplies a coefficient appropriate to the mode (linear, area, or volume); the tool does not infer material properties or convert a linear coefficient to an area/volume coefficient. Real behavior may vary with temperature, material direction, phase, constraints, moisture and geometry. Not engineering or safety advice; local browser calculation only, no uploaded data.

functions: solve Q = m·c·ΔT for heat energy, mass, specific heat capacity or temperature difference with common metric and US customary units
estimate ideal equilibrium temperature for two mixed materials using their masses and specific heat capacities
let the user enter heat lost from or added to the mixed system, with visible assumptions and copyable results

inventory.boundary: Educational sensible-heat estimate only. Assumes constant specific heat over the entered range and does not model phase change, temperature-dependent material properties, evaporation, reaction, or unentered heat transfer. Mixing assumes ideal equilibrium and user-entered heat loss. Not engineering, laboratory, or safety advice; verify material data for real applications. Values remain in the browser.

functions: solve molar concentration from amount of substance and final solution volume

estimate solute mass from target molarity, final solution volume and entered molar mass
provide an explicit final-volume example and distinguish molarity from molality

Follow chemical labels and qualified institutional safety guidance; not laboratory or medical advice.

functions: estimate pH and pOH for idealized strong acid/base concentration models and monoprotic weak acid/base equilibrium
solve weak equilibrium with mass balance and water autoionization at 25 °C
show hydrogen and hydroxide concentrations, estimated ionization and assumptions in the result
inventory.acceptance: An entered hydrogen-ion concentration of 1 × 10⁻⁷ mol/L returns pH 7 and pOH 7 in this ideal 25 °C model.
inventory.boundary: Educational ideal dilute-solution estimate only. Uses concentrations as activities; assumes strong species fully dissociate and weak species have one ionization step; fixes pKw at 14.00 for 25 °C. Does not model polyprotic acids, buffers, salts, activity coefficients, titration, temperature variation or solution interactions. Not lab, medical, food, pool or soil advice; calculations run locally without upload.

functions: calculate area and centroid coordinates for solid rectangle, solid circle, centered hollow rectangle, circular tube and triangle cross-sections
calculate centroidal Ix and Iy in the same user-selected length unit as the dimensions
report elastic section modulus about x with separate top and bottom values for an asymmetric triangle, and about y
show a clear structural-design boundary and keep all inputs in the browser

inventory.boundary: Ideal prismatic geometry only for a small set of simple shapes. Hollow sections are centered; moments are about centroidal axes parallel to the entered dimensions. Not an I-beam/section database, stress or load-capacity check, buckling analysis, connection design or code-compliance tool. Material, loads, end conditions, imperfections and safety factors are not modeled. Have structural decisions reviewed by a qualified engineer; calculations are local and inputs are not uploaded.

functions: solve exactly one missing value among wave frequency, wavelength and propagation speed using v=f×λ

offer approximate optical light-speed presets for vacuum, air, water and glass, plus custom speed for sound or other waves
show the solved value, all three values, units and the equation while keeping calculation inputs in the browser
inventory.acceptance: With frequency 100 MHz and speed 300,000,000 m/s and wavelength blank, the calculator returns 3 m; entering 2 kHz and 75 cm with speed blank returns 1,500 m/s.

secondaryIntents: solve ideal gas law for pressure volume moles temperature
functions: solve exactly one missing pressure, volume, amount of gas or absolute temperature with PV=nRT
convert common SI and customary pressure, volume and amount units while preserving physical values when units change
accept kelvin or Celsius and reject temperatures at or below absolute zero

Real gases may differ, especially at high pressure or low temperature. This is not chemical safety, vessel, process or engineering design advice; no inputs are uploaded or saved by the tool.

secondaryIntents: torque from force and lever arm

functions: calculate torque magnitude from force, lever arm distance and angle using τ = rF sin(θ)
solve for force or lever arm from known torque and the other input
convert force between N, kN and lbf, distance between m, cm, mm, ft and in, and torque between N·m, kN·m, lb·ft and lb·in
show perpendicular force and moment-arm components, direction, formula and a small lever diagram
inventory.acceptance: A 10 N perpendicular force 2 m from a pivot creates 20 N·m; at 30° it creates 10 N·m.
inventory.boundary: Ideal static moment from one force about a fixed pivot. Angle is between the pivot-to-application vector and the force; positive is counterclockwise and negative clockwise. This is not a structural, lifting, automotive or safety design tool. It does not model multiple loads, friction, deformation or dynamic systems; calculations stay in the browser.

functions: estimate elastic deflection for simply supported and cantilever beams under a centered point load or full-span uniform load
enter span, load, elastic modulus and second moment of area with explicit compatible units
show maximum deflection, location, bending moment, flexural rigidity and a sampled deflection curve
state the Euler–Bernoulli small-deflection assumptions and the educational-only design boundary
inventory.acceptance: With a simply supported 4 m beam, centered 1,000 N point load, E=200 GPa and I=8×10⁻⁶ m⁴, maximum deflection is about 0.8333 mm; zero applied load gives zero deflection.
inventory.boundary: Ideal prismatic, linearly elastic, constant-EI Euler–Bernoulli beam with small deflection and the selected textbook load/support case only. Ignores shear deformation, self-weight, multiple/off-center loads, stability, yielding, connections, lateral-torsional buckling, code limits and load combinations. Educational estimate only; never use to approve, size or certify a real structure. Ask a qualified structural engineer. All calculations run locally; no upload or server processing.

functions: calculate the required series resistance from supply voltage, LED forward voltage, series LED count and target current
round upward to a preferred E12 or E24 resistor value so the estimated current does not exceed the requested target
show the resulting current, resistor dissipation and a conservative next standard power rating
inventory.acceptance: 12 V supply, one 2 V LED and 20 mA target requires 500 Ω; E12 recommends 560 Ω, giving about 17.86 mA and 0.179 W dissipation.
inventory.boundary: Ideal DC series-circuit estimate only. It omits LED forward-voltage variation, temperature, supply tolerance, switching, wiring and component derating details; verify actual datasheets and limits. The suggested power rating is a simple 2× estimate, not a safety certification. Educational use only; not a substitute for qualified electrical review. Inputs stay in this browser.

functions: calculate volumetric flow Q = area × average velocity or solve cross-sectional area or velocity from known flow
convert area, velocity and flow rate across common metric and US customary units
estimate tank/container fill time from volume and a constant flow rate
inventory.acceptance: A 2 m² cross-section at 3 m/s gives 6 m³/s; 1 m³ fills in 16.6667 minutes at 1 L/s.
inventory.boundary: Steady incompressible-flow arithmetic only. Does not model pressure loss, friction, pipe roughness, fittings, fluid changes, pump performance, leaks, compressibility or changing tank levels. Verify real system measurements and manufacturer data; not plumbing or engineering design advice. Inputs stay in this browser.

functions: calculate Re = density × velocity × characteristic length ÷ dynamic viscosity or velocity × length ÷ kinematic viscosity
convert common SI and US customary units for density, velocity, length and viscosity
show conventional internal-pipe regime ranges while identifying external-flow classification as context-dependent
inventory.acceptance: Water at 20°C using density 998.2 kg/m³, velocity 1 m/s, length 0.05 m and dynamic viscosity 0.001002 Pa·s gives Re ≈ 49,810; zero velocity gives Re = 0.
inventory.boundary: Dimensionless educational estimate only. Pipe transition ranges around Re 2,300 and 4,000 are conventional approximations, not guarantees; geometry, entrance effects, roughness, disturbances and fluid state matter. External-flow thresholds depend on geometry and characteristic length; no universal regime is assigned. Verify inputs and use qualified engineering judgment. Inputs stay in this browser.

functions: estimate active, apparent and reactive power from line voltage, line current and power factor
switch between single-phase and balanced three-phase AC
show star/wye or delta phase voltage and current relationships
inventory.acceptance: A balanced three-phase system at 400 V line voltage, 10 A line current and PF 0.8 gives P = √3 × 400 × 10 × 0.8 ≈ 5,542.6 W.
inventory.boundary: Ideal sinusoidal AC estimate; assumes a balanced three-phase load. Power factor is treated as a magnitude and reactive power is reported unsigned. Does not model harmonics, phase imbalance, conductor sizing, protection, equipment ratings, electrical safety or code compliance. Use qualified engineering judgment for real installations. Inputs stay in this browser.

functions: solve stock aliquot and idealized diluent volume for a direct C1V1=C2V2 dilution
split a total dilution factor into equal serial steps and calculate per-step transfer and diluent volumes
support consistent user-selected concentration units and L/mL volume units with explicit assumptions
inventory.acceptance: 10 M stock to 2 M target at 1 L final volume yields 0.2 L stock and 0.8 L diluent; three equal serial steps for 10× total dilution use per-step factor 10^(1/3).
inventory.boundary: Educational arithmetic only, not a laboratory protocol or safety advice. Concentration units must match. Assumes ideal additive volumes; does not model stock purity, density, compatibility, heat, measurement uncertainty or chemical hazards. Follow the chemical safety documentation and qualified laboratory procedures.

functions: solve voltage, current, resistance and power from any two valid positive values using the DC resistive Ohm’s-law relationships
calculate equivalent resistance for a list of 2 to 20 resistors in series or parallel
show all solved values with explicit V, A, Ω and W units and a copyable result
inventory.acceptance: 12 V across 6 Ω returns 2 A and 24 W; 2 Ω, 3 Ω and 6 Ω in parallel return 1 Ω equivalent resistance.
inventory.boundary: Ideal DC resistive arithmetic only. Does not account for AC impedance, reactive components, source/internal resistance, tolerance, heating, power ratings, wiring, or electrical-code and shock/fire risks. Do not use it to certify a circuit or select safe components; verify with a qualified professional and component datasheets. Inputs stay in this browser.

functions: calculate ideal secondary voltage from primary voltage and primary/secondary turns
find the turns ratio from primary and secondary voltage
estimate secondary current from primary current, turns ratio and a user-entered efficiency
inventory.acceptance: A 2:1 primary-to-secondary turns ratio with 120 V input yields 60 V ideal secondary voltage.
inventory.boundary: Educational ideal-transformer arithmetic only; assumes sinusoidal steady-state RMS values and the turns ratio convention Ns/Np. Does not select transformer ratings or model core saturation, frequency, losses beyond a user-entered efficiency, winding resistance, inrush, isolation, wiring or shock/fire risk. Not electrical design or safety advice; consult datasheets and a qualified professional. Inputs stay in this browser.

functions: balance a supported neutral reaction and show its coefficient ratios
enter mass in grams or amount in moles for each reactant and identify the limiting reactant or tied limiting reactants
calculate theoretical moles and mass for every product using the supported molar-mass table
optionally compare actual product mass with theoretical mass to calculate percent yield and show the calculation steps
inventory.acceptance: For 2 mol H2 and 1 mol O2 in 2H2 + O2 → 2H2O, water theoretical yield is 2 mol or about 36.03 g; an actual yield of 18.015 g is 50%.
inventory.boundary: Educational stoichiometry for balanced, neutral molecular equations and elements supported by the molar-mass calculator. It does not model limiting purity, solutions, gases, equilibrium, side reactions, ionic/electron balance, kinetics, actual reaction conditions or hazards. A percent yield above 100% is shown as entered and may indicate moisture, impurities or measurement issues. Not a lab procedure or safety advice; follow qualified supervision and safety data. Inputs stay in the browser.

functions: calculate average pressure from a normal force and contact area with selectable force, area, and pressure units
estimate hydrostatic gauge pressure from user-entered fluid density, depth, and gravitational acceleration
show the selected model and converted inputs with the result so the assumptions are transparent
inventory.acceptance: 100 N divided by 2 m² returns 50 Pa; water at 1,000 kg/m³ and 1 m depth under 9.80665 m/s² returns 9,806.65 Pa gauge.
inventory.boundary: Ideal average pressure p=F/A or hydrostatic gauge pressure Δp=ρgh only. The force model assumes the entered normal force is evenly distributed over the entered area; it does not calculate stress concentrations. The liquid model assumes a static uniform-density fluid and does not include atmospheric pressure, flow, pressure loss, temperature, compressibility, vessel loads or safety ratings. Not engineering or safety advice; verify real systems with qualified professionals. Calculations run locally and inputs are not uploaded.

secondaryIntents: printed circuit board trace current capacity
functions: estimate PCB copper trace width from current, copper weight, allowable temperature rise, and internal or external layer
estimate current capacity for a specified width and copper weight using the same explicit model
show width in mil and mm and disclose the empirical model and assumptions
inventory.acceptance: zero current is rejected as not dimensionable; 2 A, 1 oz copper, 10 °C rise on an external trace returns a finite positive width estimate.
inventory.boundary: Legacy IPC-2221 empirical current/temperature-rise approximation only, using separate k values for internal and external conductors. Not IPC certification or a guarantee of safe design; it omits board stack-up, copper roughness, plating, etching, nearby planes, airflow, pulse/current duty, ambient temperature and manufacturing tolerances. Use the current applicable IPC standard, thermal simulation, and qualified engineering review for real products. Calculations run locally; inputs are not uploaded.

functions: calculate an ideal projectile path with launch speed, angle, initial height and constant gravity, without air resistance
report flight time, horizontal range, peak height, time to peak and impact speed in selected units
plot the trajectory and let the visitor replay its motion on demand, respecting reduced-motion preferences
inventory.acceptance: A 90-degree vertical launch has zero horizontal velocity and range; a 20 m/s launch at 45 degrees from ground level under 9.80665 m/s² travels about 40.79 m and reaches about 10.20 m high.
inventory.boundary: Introductory point-mass model with constant gravity and no air resistance, wind, lift, spin, obstacles or changing altitude reference. Assumes landing at height zero and upward launch angles from 0 to 90 degrees. Not a prediction for real projectiles or safety guidance. Calculation and optional animation run locally in the browser.

functions: estimate an open two-pulley belt pitch length from driver and driven diameters and center distance
calculate ideal driven RPM from pulley diameters and input RPM, including speed increases or reductions
show belt linear speed, approximate small-pulley wrap angle and a labeled local geometry sketch
inventory.acceptance: A 100 mm driver, 200 mm driven pulley, 500 mm center distance and 1,500 input RPM estimate a 1,476 mm open-belt length and 750 output RPM; equal pulleys preserve input RPM.
inventory.boundary: Approximate ideal geometry for two pulleys and one open belt only. Length is a common pitch-length approximation; it does not select a catalog belt, account for belt thickness/profile, tension, slip, wear, tolerances, idlers, crossed drives, load, power, guarding or safety. Check the manufacturer’s sizing data and a qualified professional before purchase or operation. Runs locally; inputs are not uploaded.

functions: calculate ideal LC resonant frequency, topology-specific quality factor Q and bandwidth for series or parallel RLC circuits
calculate inductive and capacitive reactance plus complex impedance magnitude and phase at a user-selected frequency
estimate RMS source current and show a local log-frequency impedance response curve around resonance
inventory.acceptance: For R=10 ohms, L=10 mH and C=1 uF, resonance is about 1,591.55 Hz; at resonance a series circuit has impedance 10 ohms and phase 0 degrees, with Q=10 and bandwidth about 159.15 Hz.
inventory.boundary: Ideal lumped, linear RLC model only, with one resistor, inductor and capacitor in the selected series or parallel topology. Does not model component tolerances, parasitics, coil resistance, source impedance, nonlinear parts, transmission lines, load coupling, safety, or certify/build a real circuit. The parallel model uses R in parallel with L and C. Verify with datasheets and a qualified professional before using real hardware; inputs stay in this browser.

functions: estimate free-space wavelength and ideal half-wave dipole or quarter-wave monopole length from operating frequency
apply an editable conductor shortening factor and show both the ideal length and a practical starting estimate
show the total dipole length, each equal dipole leg, and metric/imperial results with explicit formulas
inventory.acceptance: At 100 MHz, free-space wavelength is about 3 m and ideal half-wave dipole length is about 1.5 m total (about 0.75 m per leg) before any shortening factor.
inventory.boundary: Basic straight-conductor geometry in free space only. The adjustable factor is a starting estimate, not a universal correction or coaxial velocity factor. Feed, element diameter, ground, nearby objects and installation affect resonance and tuning. Does not predict impedance, gain, pattern, matching, legal compliance or safety; measure/tune the installed antenna and follow applicable radio and installation rules. Runs locally; no values uploaded.

functions: parse neutral molecular formulas with parentheses and hydrate separators for the elements supported by the UsefulVerse molar-mass calculator
balance reactants and products with exact rational row reduction and positive integer coefficients for supported equations; disclose when multiple-solution search is bounded
show a copyable balanced equation and reject malformed, charged or ambiguous equations that exceed the bounded local solver
inventory.acceptance: H2 + O2 -> H2O balances as 2H2 + O2 -> 2H2O; Ca(OH)2 + HCl -> CaCl2 + H2O balances as Ca(OH)2 + 2HCl -> CaCl2 + 2H2O.
inventory.boundary: Educational atom-count balancing only for supported neutral formulas; it does not handle ionic charge/electron balance, half-reactions, reaction prediction, states, mechanisms, yields or hazards. Some underdetermined equations are rejected when a small bounded search cannot establish a minimum. Check the chemistry and follow qualified laboratory safety procedures; this is not a lab protocol or safety advice. Inputs stay in this browser.

functions: calculate overall driven-to-driver tooth ratio across one to six compound stages for external gears or an uncrossed chain
estimate output RPM from input RPM and ideal output torque from optional input torque
apply an optional user-entered per-stage efficiency estimate and report direction assumptions for external gear meshes versus chain drives
inventory.acceptance: A 20-tooth driver and 40-tooth driven gear give a 2:1 reduction; 1,500 input RPM yields 750 output RPM and 10 N·m ideal input torque yields 20 N·m ideal output torque.
inventory.boundary: Ideal kinematic ratio and torque estimate only; does not design gears, check strength, tooth profile, backlash, lubrication, bearing or motor loads, belt slip, chain tension, efficiency, safety or standards. Multi-stage input assumes each driven member shares a shaft with the next stage driver. An entered efficiency is a user assumption applied per stage. Verify mechanical design with a qualified engineer and component data. Inputs stay in this browser.

functions: solve mass, volume or density when exactly two are known in kg, m³ and kg/m³
convert the result to g/cm³ and lb/ft³
estimate aggregate density for up to twelve components when their masses and volumes are supplied, explicitly assuming additive volumes
inventory.acceptance: 10 kg divided by 2 m³ gives 5 kg/m³; 10 kg at 5 kg/m³ gives 2 m³; mixture rows 2 kg, 1 m³ and 3 kg, 0.5 m³ give 5 kg total, 1.5 m³ total and 3.333333 kg/m³.
inventory.boundary: Positive scalar arithmetic only. Component volumes are assumed additive; this is not valid for every blend, dissolved material, porous material or compressible fluid. No material identification, temperature/pressure correction, purity, safety, engineering certification or lab protocol. Inputs remain in this browser.

functions: calculate swept cylinder volume from bore and stroke in metric or imperial dimensions
combine chamber, head-gasket, deck and piston crown volumes to estimate clearance volume and static compression ratio
show per-cylinder and total engine displacement for one to sixteen cylinders, with explicit piston dish/dome sign convention
inventory.acceptance: A cylinder with 9 cc swept volume and 1 cc clearance volume has a 10:1 static compression ratio; bore 86 mm and stroke 86 mm with chamber volume set equal to one ninth of the swept volume gives 10:1 within rounding.
inventory.boundary: Static geometric estimate only. Does not model dynamic compression, cam timing, boost, trapped volume, fuel, detonation, thermal expansion, machining tolerances, gasket crush, clearances under operation, component strength or engine safety. Piston crown volume is positive for a dish and negative for a dome. Verify measurements and consult engine specifications or a qualified builder. Inputs stay in this browser.

functions: convert Gregorian civil dates to the browser’s built-in Hebrew calendar
convert valid Hebrew year/month/day values back to Gregorian civil dates
show Hebrew leap years with Adar I and Adar II as separate months
state that Hebrew calendar days begin at sunset and are not translated to local sunset times
inventory.acceptance: Gregorian 2024-03-11 converts to 1 Adar II 5784; 2023-09-16 converts to 1 Tishri 5784. Both directions round-trip, and Adar II is only selectable in Hebrew leap years.
inventory.boundary: Uses the Hebrew calendar implemented by the visitor’s browser Intl.DateTimeFormat, with Gregorian output restricted to years 1–9999. No local sunset/time-zone calculation, holiday lookup, moon observation, religious ruling or network service. Browser calendar-data differences and community conventions are possible; dates are civil midnight dates while the Hebrew day begins at sunset.

functions: calculate the nonnegative absolute value of a signed number
solve equations of the form |a·x + b| = c, including zero and impossible targets
solve strict and inclusive linear absolute value inequalities as points, intervals or exterior rays
show the solution set in interval notation and on a number line
inventory.acceptance: |x| = 3 returns x = −3 or x = 3; |2x − 4| ≤ 6 returns [−1, 5]; |x| > 3 returns (−∞, −3) ∪ (3, ∞). Negative equation targets have no solution; constant expressions return all real numbers or none as appropriate.
inventory.boundary: Supports only |a·x + b| compared with one real target, plus the absolute value of one number. Inputs are bounded to ±10¹². It is not a general symbolic algebra system and does not solve quadratics, nested absolute values, multiple variables or arbitrary expressions. All arithmetic runs locally.

functions: enter household members and weekly chores with optional 1–5 effort points
generate a one-to-twelve-week Monday-start schedule that rotates tasks while balancing weighted assignments
show each person’s total effort points and the schedule’s load spread
print the schedule or export a CSV without saving names or tasks online
inventory.acceptance: With three members, chores weighted 3, 2 and 1, and four weeks, every chore appears once per week; Monday dates advance by seven days; assignments rotate and total weighted load remains within three points. Invalid duplicate members/tasks, non-Monday dates and effort outside 1–5 are rejected.
inventory.boundary: A weekly household chore rotation planner, not a calendar sync, reminder, reward system or assessment of actual effort. Effort points are only user-selected balancing weights; equal points do not guarantee equal time or difficulty. Data remains in the current tab unless the visitor prints or exports CSV.

functions: turn a measurable outcome into a dated plan with a baseline, target, start date and deadline
add dated milestones inside the plan window and mark each milestone complete
record dated progress measurements and calculate directional progress toward the target
save one active plan locally in the current browser and download a JSON backup
inventory.acceptance: A plan starting 2026-02-01 and due 2026-06-01 accepts milestones on or after the start and on or before the deadline; it rejects a milestone before the start or after the deadline. Baseline 10, target 20 and current 15 reports 50% progress; a decrease target of 20 to 10 with current 15 also reports 50%.
inventory.boundary: A private, single-plan goal tracker, not a task list, calendar sync, reminder service, coaching system or guarantee of achievement. Data is stored only in this browser when storage is available and can be cleared by the browser. Export a JSON backup to keep a copy. Progress is a simple linear comparison to the chosen baseline and target; it is not a measure of effort or probability of success.

functions: build a branching idea tree from one central topic
edit, add, remove, move and reorder nodes
collapse branches and undo or redo up to 30 recent edits
export the full map as SVG or a portable JSON backup
inventory.acceptance: Create a root with two branches and one child; move that child to the other branch and verify the hierarchy and export. Attempt to move an ancestor below its descendant and reject the cycle without changing the map. Undo and redo the valid move exactly.
inventory.boundary: A local tree editor for brainstorming, not a linear process diagram, collaborative canvas or cloud-synced workspace. Ideas remain in page memory unless the user exports a JSON file. SVG text is escaped and output is static.

functions: record one self-rated 1–5 mood check-in per calendar day with optional emotion tags and a private note
browse check-ins in an accessible month calendar and edit or delete a day
summarize recorded values using a non-clinical weekly average and mood distribution without interpreting mental health
save only after explicit per-session consent, export a JSON backup and validate/import it locally
inventory.acceptance: With storage consent off, a check-in exists only in page memory and is absent after reload; with consent on, one check-in can be restored from this browser, edited by date, removed, exported and imported without duplicate dates.
inventory.boundary: A private self-reflection log, not a diagnosis, treatment, medical record or crisis service. Mood scores are personal labels and summaries describe only recorded entries; they do not infer causes or clinical trends. Inputs stay in memory unless the visitor explicitly enables this browser’s local storage; no account, sync, analytics payload or upload is added. Shared devices and browser backups can expose locally stored notes.

functions: write multiple dated journal entries with titles and optional tags
search entry titles, body text and tags and filter by a date range entirely in this browser
optionally save entries in this browser with a clear warning that browser storage is not a secure vault
export/import a validated portable JSON backup, or optionally encrypt a backup with the browser Web Crypto API and a user-held passphrase
inventory.acceptance: Create two dated entries with overlapping text; title/body/tag search and a date filter return only matches; edit and delete affect the stable entry ID. A plain JSON backup round-trips. An encrypted AES-GCM backup decrypts with the right passphrase and fails with a wrong one or altered ciphertext. Data is not saved unless storage is explicitly enabled; disabling it removes the persisted copy but keeps the active tab copy in memory.
inventory.boundary: A single-device personal writing tool, not a cloud-synced diary, account, reminder service, password manager, therapy or clinical product. Browser persistence is plain browser storage and can be exposed by access to the browser profile; it is never described as encrypted. Only an explicitly exported encrypted backup uses AES-GCM with a key derived locally from a passphrase; the passphrase is not transmitted or stored. Losing it makes that encrypted backup unrecoverable. All work is local; no server, analytics payload or API is added.

functions: create a dated multi-day trip and manually schedule activities, meals, transport, stays and reservations
store each stop’s local wall-clock date and time, place, booking reference and notes; edit or delete by stable ID
flag actual same-day time overlaps and separately warn when consecutive stops leave less than the user-selected connection buffer
export calendar events as an ICS file, export/import a validated JSON backup, or use the browser print dialog
inventory.acceptance: A 3-day trip accepts stops only inside the date range; same-day events 09:00–10:00 and 09:45–10:30 report a 15-minute overlap, while 10:40 after a 10:30 finish reports a 10-minute gap when the selected buffer is 30 minutes. Editing keeps the same ID and stop count. JSON round-trips. ICS uses escaped, folded CRLF lines and floating local times; no time-zone conversion, bookings, routing, travel-time estimate or network request is claimed.
inventory.boundary: A manually entered itinerary organizer, not a booking service, live flight/hotel feed, map, navigation or route optimizer. Times are floating local wall-clock values; users must confirm the destination time zone and calendar behavior. Overnight items are not supported. Connection warnings compare schedule times with a user-entered buffer; they do not estimate travel time. Itinerary data stays in this browser tab unless the visitor explicitly enables this browser’s unencrypted local storage or exports a file. No travel API or paid service is used.

functions: parse bounded integer-coefficient polynomial expressions in x up to degree 20
show exact quotient and remainder using reduced integer fractions
show each quotient term, subtraction and new remainder in long-division order
copy a worked result and load the x² − 1 divided by x − 1 example
inventory.acceptance: Dividing x^2 - 1 by x - 1 returns quotient x + 1 and remainder 0 with two valid subtraction steps. Dividing x^2 by 2x + 1 returns quotient x/2 - 1/4 and remainder 1/4. Zero divisors, malformed terms and degrees above 20 are rejected.
inventory.boundary: Polynomial long division in one variable x with integer input coefficients and exact rational quotient/remainder. It is distinct from integer long division and from factorization, derivatives or integrals. No arbitrary symbolic functions, decimal/fraction input coefficients, multiple variables or CAS are claimed. Maximum degree 20, 64 terms and 256 characters per expression; all calculations are local.

functions: solve for initial amount, remaining amount, elapsed time or half-life from the other three values
show percent remaining and elapsed half-lives
use a selected shared time unit and an example that halves 100 to 50 after one half-life
inventory.acceptance: With initial amount 100, half-life 5730 years and elapsed time 5730 years, the remaining amount is 50 (50%). Solving elapsed time from 100 to 25 with half-life 10 returns 20 time units.
inventory.boundary: Educational exponential-decay mathematics only. It does not provide medical, radiation-dose, exposure, shielding, contamination, safety or handling guidance. Initial/remaining amounts and half-life must be positive; elapsed time may be zero; decay remaining amount cannot exceed initial amount. Time inputs use the same selected unit. Non-finite and results outside the representable numeric range are rejected. Runs locally without upload or paid services.

secondaryIntents: compare mortgage points and interest rates
functions: compare two lender-quoted rates for the same principal and term
model points as a cash upfront cost equal to a user-entered percentage of principal
calculate monthly payments, full-term interest, payoff horizon balances and net benefit
show payment-only and balance-inclusive break-even months separately
inventory.acceptance: For a positive points cost and identical rates, monthly payment and interest savings are zero, the horizon net benefit equals the negative upfront cost, and neither break-even is falsely reported.
inventory.boundary: An educational comparison, not financial advice, a mortgage offer or a loan estimate. Rates are user-provided; no lender discount is assumed. Points are modeled as cash paid at closing equal to a percentage of principal. Taxes, deductibility, other closing costs, escrow, insurance, variable rates and lender-specific rules are excluded. Principal, APR, term and comparison horizon are bounded; calculations run locally.

functions: calculate area from two parallel bases and perpendicular height
derive both side lengths and perimeter from the top-base horizontal offset
show a responsive geometric sketch and keep every length in one selected unit
inventory.acceptance: Bases 6 and 4, height 3 and top offset 1 return area 15 and equal side lengths √10; invalid offsets that make the side edges cross are rejected.
inventory.boundary: A convex trapezoid with one pair of parallel horizontal bases. All entered lengths must use the same selected unit. The offset determines the non-parallel side lengths; the diagram is illustrative, not scale-accurate. Geometry only, not a construction specification.

functions: calculate Fajr, sunrise, Dhuhr, Asr, sunset, Maghrib and Isha locally from a Gregorian date, manually entered coordinates and an explicit UTC offset
select a published angle-based method, standard or Hanafi Asr, optional Makkah Ramadan Isha interval, and an explicit higher-latitude adjustment
report unavailable polar sunrise/sunset honestly and apply high-latitude twilight fallback only when the selected method requires it
show the selected assumptions and copy the resulting local-clock schedule
inventory.acceptance: For New York (40.7128, -74.0060), 2026-03-20, UTC−4, ISNA and standard Asr, return an ordered same-day schedule with Dhuhr 13:04 and sunrise 07:00 (minute-rounded); UTC−5 moves each clock time back one hour without changing solar intervals. On 2026-06-21 at latitude 89°, sunrise/sunset are unavailable rather than fabricated.
inventory.boundary: Approximate astronomical schedule using the stated method, manually entered coordinates and civil UTC offset; it is not an official local mosque timetable or religious ruling. Methods can differ by community, authority, elevation, local convention and precaution. User must verify method/offset with a trusted local authority. No auto-location, geocoding, notification, adhan audio, Ramadan calendar, or API. For twilight that does not occur, a user-selected high-latitude estimate is explicitly marked; no estimate is silently presented as observation.

secondaryIntents: crown molding miter and bevel calculator
functions: calculate a symmetric simple miter from an inside corner angle
calculate compound miter and bevel magnitudes for flat crown molding using an explicit spring-angle convention
show an accessible angle diagram, worked example, copyable settings and limits
inventory.acceptance: A 90° inside corner gives a 45° simple miter. With flat crown molding and a 38° spring angle measured from its wall-side back, compound settings are approximately 31.62° miter and 33.86° bevel.
inventory.boundary: Geometry only. The compound formula assumes flat crown molding and spring angle measured from the wall-side back; other conventions or molding orientations can differ. Outputs are unsigned magnitudes and do not identify left/right saw orientation. Verify the profile, saw manual and a test piece before cutting; not construction or safety advice.

functions: estimate resistive voltage drop for copper or aluminum conductors from one-way length, current, cross-sectional area and supply voltage
support DC two-conductor, single-phase AC and balanced three-phase AC modes with optional power factor
show volts, percentage, estimated load voltage and explicit calculation assumptions
inventory.acceptance: Zero route length yields zero drop; for 20 A over 30 m one-way in 2.5 mm² copper at 230 V single-phase and power factor 1, resistive drop is about 8.27 V (3.60%).
inventory.boundary: Reference-resistivity, resistive-only estimate at 20°C, not wire sizing or electrical safety advice. Omits conductor heating, AC reactance, harmonics, connectors, installation conditions, ampacity, overcurrent protection and local codes. Three-phase assumes balanced load. Qualified electrician must verify design and local requirements.

functions: rectangular deck area in metric or imperial units
board rows from actual board width and gap
stock board count with a user-entered waste allowance and material price
support-line and simplified fastener estimate from user-entered spacing
approximate butt-joint count when stock boards are shorter than the deck run
inventory.acceptance: For a 16 × 12 ft deck with 5.5 in boards, 0.25 in gaps, 16 ft stock boards, 16 in support spacing and 10% waste: 26 rows, 29 stock boards, 13 support lines and 676 fasteners at two per crossing. With 8 ft stock boards, report 26 planned row joints.
inventory.boundary: Simple surface-material estimate only. It does not design joists, beams, posts, foundations, stairs, guards, drainage, permits or code compliance, and it does not generate a cut map. Board-end joints must be planned and supported; verify materials and construction with a qualified builder.

functions: convert horizontal projected roof area to sloped roof area using rise and run
optional material allowance for cuts and waste
roofing squares and whole shingle bundles from a user-selected bundles-per-square rate
optional cost from a user-entered bundle price
inventory.acceptance: For 1,200 ft² projected area and 6:12 pitch, sloped roof area is greater than 1,200 ft²; with 10% extra and 3 bundles per 100 ft², round up to 45 bundles.
inventory.boundary: Material estimate only. Roof dimensions, layers, valley/ridge details, ventilation, underlayment, fasteners, flashing, product coverage, local codes and safe access are not evaluated; verify measurements and manufacturer coverage with a qualified roofer.

functions: wall and optional ceiling area for repeated rectangular rooms
deduct a user-entered opening area per room
custom sheet dimensions and extra-material allowance
whole-sheet count, approximate joint-seam length, screw estimate and optional sheet budget

handle exponential shifts of supported polynomial and trigonometric terms and show the region of convergence
invert common simple poles, repeated shifted real poles and standard sine/cosine partial fractions
explain accepted notation and reject expressions outside the implemented table rather than returning guessed algebra
inventory.acceptance: The forward transform of 1 is 1/s; the inverse transform of 1/s is 1; the forward transform of exp(-2*t) is 1/(s+2) with Re(s)>-2.
inventory.boundary: Bounded unilateral Laplace transform table, not a general symbolic algebra system. Forward syntax supports at most 12 terms and powers through t^8; inverse mode requires one already-separated partial-fraction term per line. No automatic partial-fraction decomposition, arbitrary products, piecewise/distribution inputs or numerical inversion. All calculations run locally without a remote math service.

functions: add and subtract 2D or 3D vectors
calculate dot and cross products, including the signed z-component for 2D cross products
calculate vector magnitudes, unit vectors, angle in degrees and projection of A onto B
show related magnitudes and dot product alongside the selected operation
inventory.acceptance: For A=(1,0,0) and B=(0,1,0), the dot product is 0 and the cross product is (0,0,1); in 2D the same cross product is the signed scalar z-component 1.
inventory.boundary: Dimensionless component arithmetic; components must use compatible units if they represent physical quantities. Each component is limited to ±1,000,000,000. Angles are in degrees. Zero vectors cannot be normalized or used to define an angle; projection onto a zero vector is undefined. All calculations run locally without data lookups, APIs or server processing.

functions: estimate distinct real roots for cubic and quartic polynomials from coefficients
report estimated multiplicities and absolute residuals for each displayed root
sort distinct roots numerically and identify when non-real roots are not shown
provide an example and reject unsupported degree, missing values, unsafe coefficient sizes and poorly conditioned leading terms
inventory.acceptance: For x³ − 1 = 0, report the real root x = 1 with multiplicity 1 and a near-zero residual; for x⁴ − 5x² + 4 = 0, report −2, −1, 1 and 2.
inventory.boundary: Numerical real roots only for degree 3 or 4; not a symbolic solver and does not calculate complex roots or exact algebraic factors. Coefficients are limited to ±1,000,000 and the leading coefficient must be at least 1e-12 of the largest coefficient. Near-multiple roots can be ill-conditioned; residuals expose approximation quality but do not certify a root. All computation runs locally without APIs or server processing.

functions: calculate a transparent linear energy-equivalent scenario from a user-entered weight goal and daily deficit
support kilograms and pounds
show modeled energy equivalent, estimated scenario timeline and implied weekly rate
return no projected change when the entered deficit is zero
explain why the simplified linear rule is not a physiological forecast and link to official sources
inventory.acceptance: For 80 kg to 70 kg at an entered 500 kcal/day, the simple 7,700 kcal/kg scenario is 77,000 kcal and 154 days; a zero deficit produces zero modeled weekly change and no finite timeline.
inventory.boundary: Educational arithmetic only, not a body-weight prediction, diet plan, calorie target or medical advice. The static energy-per-mass rule does not model changing metabolism, body composition, medicines or individual response; do not use it to choose a deficit. Runs locally and retains no inputs.

functions: split 2–60 unique participant names into 2–12 balanced teams
keep selected participant pairs on different teams
create a reproducible randomized result from an optional seed
copy a readable result or download a CSV locally

inventory.boundary: A local randomized group split, not a cryptographic lottery or a guarantee of mathematically uniform assignments. Constraints are searched with a fixed work budget; a complex case may request simpler constraints instead of proving that no split exists. Names are not uploaded or saved.

functions: estimate bricks from wall dimensions and actual brick size plus mortar joint
deduct repeated rectangular openings and show approximate courses and average bricks per course
apply configurable waste and wall wythes
estimate mortar volume and optional bag count from user-entered bag yield
inventory.acceptance: For a 10 ft × 8 ft wall with modular 7.625 × 2.25 in bricks, a 3/8 in joint, one 3 × 7 ft opening and 5% waste, the estimated order is lower than for the same closed wall; with zero waste, two wythes double the brick and mortar estimate.
inventory.boundary: Planning estimate for a flat, rectangular wall only. It does not create a bond/layout or cut plan, model corners, lintels, reinforcement, waste reuse, structural loads, moisture, code, or mortar mix. Brick dimensions and joint size are editable; openings are deducted by area, so placement and course interruptions are not modeled. Check manufacturer coverage and consult a qualified mason. All arithmetic stays in this browser.

functions: calculate geometric rafter length from building span and roof rise or pitch
account for ridge-board thickness and optional horizontal eave overhang
show the roof slope and plumb-cut angle with an accessible geometry sketch
support metric and imperial units without mixing them
inventory.acceptance: For a 20 ft span, 6 ft rise, 1.5 in ridge board and no overhang, horizontal run is 9.9375 ft; adding a 1 ft horizontal overhang increases the rafter length.
inventory.boundary: Geometry estimate for a straight, symmetric roof only. It does not size structural members or calculate birdsmouth/seat cuts, tail details, connections, load capacity, code compliance or material waste. Verify dimensions and have a qualified professional review construction plans. Inputs stay in this browser.

functions: estimate full-width carpet cuts and seams for a rectangular room from roll width
compare roll orientations and calculate material length for the selected pile direction
support identical rooms, metric/imperial dimensions and a configurable cutting allowance
show why roll-width leftovers mean purchased area exceeds floor area

inventory.boundary: Planning estimate for rectangular rooms and plain broadloom carpet only. It does not create an installer-ready cutting diagram or account for alcoves, stairs, doorways, pattern matching, pile shading, defects, joins between rooms or reusable offcuts. Verify roll width, pile direction, pattern and installation requirements with the supplier/installer. Inputs stay in this browser.

functions: estimate rectangular tank capacity from internal dimensions
subtract the unfilled top air gap and an entered solid share of the substrate layer
show usable water in litres and US/imperial gallons
estimate water mass in kilograms and pounds without including the tank, stand or decorations

inventory.boundary: Planning estimate for rectangular tanks only. Use inside dimensions. Substrate solid share is a user assumption; rocks, filters, glass thickness, decorations, supports and actual load capacity are not calculated. Water density is approximated as 1 kg/L. Check the tank maker’s guidance; all arithmetic stays in this browser.

functions: estimate seed quantity from lawn area and a user-entered product rate
accept metric or imperial area and two seeding-rate units
split the total into a two-variety mix whose shares must add to 100%
optionally round up to whole bags from a user-entered package size

functions: add resistance contributions for user-entered layers in series
multiply each layer value by its repeated quantity
convert between US R-value and metric RSI

inventory.acceptance: A layer with R-2 in series with a layer with R-3 totals R-5; metric inputs RSI 1 and RSI 2 total RSI 3.

Real wall or roof performance can differ because of framing, thermal bridges, gaps, moisture, installation and other parallel heat-flow paths. Does not recommend materials, thickness, code compliance or building design. Use tested product data and local requirements; all calculations run in this browser.

functions: estimate stud positions along a straight wall using the entered maximum spacing
place supported positions at both wall ends and the edges of up to three positioned openings
calculate stud and top/bottom plate linear material using entered row counts
accept separate units for wall dimensions and stud spacing

functions: estimate energy and cost for up to four appliances from rated power and usage schedule
accept W or kW, quantity, hours per active day, and active days in a billing period
apply a user-entered price per kWh and optional fixed charge for that same period
show each appliance and total period energy, energy charge, fixed charge, and average daily energy
inventory.acceptance: One 1000 W appliance running 1 hour per day for one day at 0.20 per kWh uses 1 kWh and costs 0.20 before fixed charges.

All calculations run locally in this browser.

functions: estimate a blended carbon-to-nitrogen ratio from up to four user-entered materials and wet masses
account for each material moisture, dry-matter carbon fraction and C:N ratio
show wet mass, dry mass, water, carbon, nitrogen and resulting mix moisture
optionally estimate water to add or moisture to remove for a user-entered target

functions: calculate nitrogen, phosphate-equivalent and potash-equivalent mass from a user-entered fertilizer amount and guaranteed-analysis percentages

accept batch or area-rate inputs without recommending an application rate
