Does not recommend rates, products, crops, timing or nutrient targets; does not assess soil, runoff, local rules or plant suitability. Follow product label and local professional guidance. All calculations run locally in this browser.

functions: add, subtract, multiply and divide complex numbers in rectangular form
convert rectangular and polar forms with degrees or radians
calculate modulus and principal argument
list every nth root for integer degrees from 2 to 12

inventory.boundary: Educational fixed-rate bond estimate, not investment advice or a market quote. Assumes regular fixed coupon dates, principal repaid at maturity and nominal annual yield compounded at the chosen payment frequency. Excludes accrued interest, clean/dirty price conventions, fees, taxes, defaults, calls, inflation, reinvestment and market day-count conventions. functions: calculate kinetic energy from mass and speed
calculate gravitational potential energy relative to an explicitly chosen zero-height reference

show the assumed gravitational acceleration and total mechanical energy without modeling losses
inventory.acceptance: A 2 kg object moving at 3 m/s has 9 J of kinetic energy; at zero reference height its gravitational potential energy is 0 J.

It ignores friction, air resistance, rotation and relativistic effects. Gravity is entered by the user (9.80665 m/s² is the example default); no location-based value is inferred. inventory.boundary: One-dimensional classical two-body model only. Assumes no net external impulse during impact; restitution is bounded to 0–1. Does not model angles, rotation, shape, deformation detail, relativistic effects or real material data. This educational estimate is not an engineering or safety assessment. All values stay in this browser.

functions: decode standard 4-, 5- and 6-band resistor colors into ohms and tolerance

It does not infer component type, power rating, circuit suitability, safety or real measured resistance. Band colors may vary physically; verify the actual component marking and datasheet. functions: solve acceleration from initial and final velocity over time
solve elapsed time from two velocities and constant acceleration
solve final velocity or displacement from initial velocity, acceleration and time
show displacement and final position using metric or imperial units

inventory.boundary: Uses one-dimensional constant acceleration with signed velocity and acceleration. Time must be positive. The result does not model changing acceleration, drag, rotation, relativistic effects or engineering/safety suitability. Calculations stay in this browser.

functions: calculate the maximum static friction from the normal force and static coefficient
compare downslope gravity plus an applied force with the static threshold
when sliding or already moving, calculate kinetic friction and net force
accept either a known normal force or mass and incline angle; convert N, kN and lbf inputs

inventory.boundary: Ideal rigid-body Coulomb friction on one surface. Static friction adjusts up to μsN; kinetic friction is μkN and opposes the specified or predicted motion. The incline model assumes uniform gravity and a straight plane; it excludes deformation, rolling, changing coefficients, vibration, air resistance and material lookup. Coefficients are user inputs, not recommendations for safety or engineering design. Calculations run locally in this browser.

functions: solve force, mass or acceleration from the other two using F = m × a

convert force between N, kN and lbf, mass between kg and lb, and acceleration between m/s² and ft/s²
show a proportional force-arrow diagram with direction and a zero-force state

inventory.boundary: Ideal one-dimensional Newtonian mechanics. Signed forces are collinear and positive/negative indicate direction; this does not resolve vector components, friction, torque, changing mass or structural/safety suitability. Unit conversions use standard factors. Calculations run locally in this browser.

functions: calculate shaft power from torque and RPM or solve for torque or RPM from the other two values
convert torque between N·m and lb·ft and power between W, kW, mechanical hp and metric PS

functions: create a printable service or maintenance work order with customer, location, contact, assignee, issue and scheduled dates, job summary and notes

functions: convert valid Gregorian dates to a deterministic tabular Hijri date and back

Gregorian range is 622–9999 CE; Hijri years are bounded to 1–10000 AH. Conversion runs locally and is not religious guidance.

functions: combine 1 to 20 capacitor values in series or parallel
convert the equivalent capacitance to a selected shared unit
optionally calculate total charge and stored energy from source voltage

functions: calculate τ = R·C with Ω/kΩ/MΩ and F/mF/μF/nF/pF units

secondaryIntents: waist circumference to hip circumference ratio

functions: estimate adult total body water in litres from age, height and weight using either published Watson equation variant

functions: calculate NE555 astable high time, low time, period, frequency and two clearly distinguished duty percentages from RA, RB and capacitance

functions: estimate real Fourier coefficients from 4–128 equally spaced numeric samples spanning one period without repeating the endpoint

functions: find the least nonnegative modular inverse for signed integers
explain existence using the greatest common divisor
show exact Euclidean quotients, remainders and Bezout coefficients

functions: enter 2–8 portfolio holdings and user-chosen target percentages
estimate each holding’s target value from the entered portfolio total
optionally split a new contribution using those target weights
show each holding’s target-minus-current difference and a copyable summary
inventory.acceptance: For a 10,000 portfolio with target weights of 60% and 40%, target values are 6,000 and 4,000 and the weights total 100%; an optional 4,000 contribution is split into 2,400 and 1,600.
inventory.boundary: Arithmetic for user-entered portfolio values and target weights only. It does not recommend an allocation, identify securities, forecast returns, model taxes/fees, place trades or assess suitability. Target-minus-current differences are not trading instructions. Values stay in the browser and no account, API or upload is used.

functions: parse conventional parentheses notation for the repeating block
convert repeating decimals to exact reduced fractions using integer arithmetic
show the exact subtraction components and optional mixed-number form
bound whole, non-repeating and repeating digits to keep calculations safe

inventory.boundary: Handles recurring decimal notation with the repeat in parentheses, not finite decimals, arbitrary typed expressions, or general fraction arithmetic. Accepts 1–18 repeating digits, up to 18 non-repeating digits and 12 whole-number digits. The exact calculation is local and uses BigInt; no API, account or upload.

functions: plot a curve from separate x(t) and y(t) expressions using a shared parameter t
set the parameter interval and sample resolution with bounded inputs
support arithmetic, powers, pi, e and a documented whitelist of common real functions without evaluating JavaScript
export sampled t, x and y coordinates as a local CSV file

inventory.boundary: Numerical parametric plotting only. Uses radians and finite floating-point samples; it does not provide symbolic simplification, implicit curves, proof of continuity, or reliable asymptote detection. Expressions are parsed by a bounded local parser, never eval, and are not uploaded. Coordinates outside the display range are omitted; verify important results independently.

functions: decompose a bounded rectangular matrix A into compact U, singular values, and V transpose
estimate numerical rank with a documented floating-point tolerance
reconstruct the original matrix and report Frobenius residual and relative error
download decomposition components and reconstruction as CSV files locally
inventory.acceptance: For a diagonal matrix diag(3,2), returns singular values 3 and 2 and reconstructs the input with negligible relative error.
inventory.boundary: Numerical SVD for rectangular matrices from 2×2 to 8×8 and finite values within ±1,000,000. Uses a Jacobi eigensolver on a scaled Gram matrix; near-singular values and rank depend on floating-point tolerance. The returned compact factors reconstruct the input numerically; this is not an exact symbolic proof or a certified high-precision result. Data stays in the browser.

functions: calculate Spearman rho as Pearson correlation applied to paired ranks
handle tied values by assigning their average ranks
show each input pair and its ranks for transparent checking
export the local result table as CSV
inventory.acceptance: For pairs (1,10), (2,20), (3,30), returns rho=1; for x values (1,1,3,4), returns average ranks (1.5,1.5,3,4).
inventory.boundary: Descriptive Spearman rank correlation for 2–500 paired finite numeric observations bounded by ±1,000,000,000,000. Ties use average ranks. Rho is undefined if either variable is constant. This tool does not calculate a p-value, confidence interval or prove causation; inference depends on study design and assumptions. Inputs remain in the browser.

functions: compare paired before/after values with the two-sided Wilcoxon signed-rank test
exclude zero differences and assign average ranks to tied absolute differences
use an exact sign-flip distribution for up to 25 nonzero pairs and a continuity-corrected normal approximation above that threshold
show positive and negative rank sums, zero/tied counts, p-value, method, and a local CSV of ranked pairs
inventory.acceptance: If every before/after pair is identical, report zero nonzero differences and a dedicated no-test result instead of inventing a p-value.
inventory.boundary: For 2–500 paired finite values within ±1,000,000,000,000. Differences are after minus before; zero differences are omitted from ranking. Exact two-sided p-values use the sign-flip distribution of average ranks for at most 25 nonzero pairs; larger samples use a normal approximation with continuity correction. The inference assumes an appropriate paired design and symmetric differences under the null; it is not a causal claim or medical advice. Inputs remain in the browser.

functions: compare parsed JSON structures while ignoring object key order
compare arrays by position or match object records by a unique string or number property
list added, removed and changed values with readable paths
copy the summary or export a local JSON Patch document
inventory.acceptance: Objects with the same values but different key order show no differences; a changed nested value is reported at its path and the generated patch transforms the original document.
inventory.boundary: Compares valid JSON only; it does not compare comments, formatting or source lines. Documents are limited to 200,000 characters each, nesting to 64 levels, visited values to 20,000 per document and displayed changes to 500. ID matching requires every item in each compared array to have a unique string/number key. Exported JSON Patch uses array indexes (RFC 6902 operations). Input remains local; no upload or API.

functions: encode text as exact UTF-8 bytes displayed as eight-bit binary groups
decode whitespace-separated or compact complete binary bytes as strict UTF-8 text
preserve accented characters, combining sequences, line breaks, emoji and a leading byte-order mark
copy or download the local conversion result and optionally group output bytes with spaces
inventory.acceptance: Converting ñ produces UTF-8 bytes C3 B1 (11000011 10110001), and decoding those groups returns ñ; a multibyte emoji also round-trips without byte loss.
inventory.boundary: Converts plain text and UTF-8 bytes, not integers between numeric bases, ASCII code points, or arbitrary encodings. Binary input may contain whitespace but must contain only 0/1 bits in complete 8-bit bytes and decode as strictly valid UTF-8. Text is limited to 20,000 UTF-16 code units; binary is limited to 160,000 bits. Uses browser TextEncoder/TextDecoder only; no API, upload or server processing.

functions: decode one local X.509 PEM/base64 certificate or select a DER file

compute a SHA-256 fingerprint of the exact certificate bytes
copy a plain-text summary without uploading or storing the certificate

inventory.boundary: Decodes fields only; does not verify signatures, trust chains, hostnames, revocation, identity, or safety. It does not fetch URLs or remote issuer certificates. One certificate, maximum 1 MiB; DER is supported through a local file and PEM/base64 DER through paste. Uses bounded local ASN.1 parsing and Web Crypto SHA-256; no API, upload or server processing.

secondaryIntents: convert xml to json with arrays
functions: convert JSON to XML and XML to JSON locally in either direction
map object properties to elements, arrays to repeated elements, and repeated child names back to arrays
map JSON @attribute and #text keys to XML attributes and text using a selectable root name
copy or download JSON/XML output with readable indentation and clear error messages

inventory.boundary: JSON arrays become repeated elements; a top-level array is wrapped in the selected root with item child elements. Attributes use @name and text uses #text. XML text becomes JSON strings, so numbers/booleans, null versus empty values, mixed-content order, comments, processing instructions, CDATA boundaries and original formatting are not guaranteed to round-trip. XML-generated JSON preserves XML names; JSON-generated XML accepts simple ASCII names only (no namespaces). Input is limited to 200,000 characters, depth 64 and 20,000 visited values/elements; arrays are limited to 5,000 entries. DTD and entity declarations are blocked; no external fetch, upload, API or server processing.

functions: convert a top-level JSON array or choose a named array inside an object, with a one-row root-object option
flatten nested objects into escaped dotted column paths and keep nested arrays as readable JSON text
preview a bounded sample and create one local XLSX worksheet without running formula-like strings
preserve numeric-looking JSON strings such as 001 as text and keep JSON numeric values numeric
inventory.acceptance: In the records dataset, the string identifier "001" remains "001" in the XLSX cell, nested profile.city becomes a column, number 12.5 remains numeric, and a string beginning = is stored as inert inline text.
inventory.boundary: Browser-only JSON-to-XLSX export, not a spreadsheet editor, formula evaluator, or full data-model converter. Supports one worksheet and array/object/scalar JSON values; named arrays are top-level object properties only. Nested objects flatten to dotted headers (dots and backslashes in original keys are escaped); arrays inside records remain compact JSON text. Duplicate JSON object keys follow JSON.parse behavior. Input stays on-device; no upload, API, fetch, storage, or formula execution. Limits: 2 MB input, 50,000 values, depth 32, 20,000 records, 200 columns, 200,000 cells, 32,000 characters per cell and 12 MiB generated workbook. Spreadsheet apps may apply their own display formatting to numeric cells; strings are emitted as explicit text cells.

functions: read one selected local file and encode its bytes as Base64 or a MIME-labelled data URI

preview common raster images from a local object URL without interpreting SVG or HTML as a preview
switch between raw Base64 and data-URI output without rereading or uploading the file

inventory.boundary: Encodes bytes from a user-selected local file; it does not encode text, fetch remote URLs, decode Base64, upload, store, or execute the output. MIME comes from the browser file metadata and falls back to application/octet-stream; it does not verify the true file format. Only PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP, BMP and AVIF are displayed in an image preview; SVG and active document types are never embedded in the page preview. One file up to 2 MiB. A 2 MiB file produces about 2.67 MiB of Base64 text and needs additional browser memory while encoding or copying.

functions: paste CSV text or open one local CSV file and detect comma, semicolon, tab or pipe delimiters
choose whether the first record is a header and edit cells or column names in a paginated grid
assign a review type (text, decimal number, ISO date or Boolean) to each column and flag non-matching non-empty cells without converting their values
search rows, add or remove rows and columns, and undo or redo up to 50 local edits
export as correctly escaped UTF-8 CSV with a selected delimiter and optional BOM

Column types are user-selected checks: blank values are ignored; decimal numbers use a dot and optional exponent, dates require valid YYYY-MM-DD, and Boolean values accept true/false/0/1. Exports UTF-8, optionally with BOM; files and edits stay in the current browser session until exported. Keep a backup of important source data.

functions: infer TypeScript interfaces, C# classes and Java model classes from pasted JSON

keep input and generated models in the browser without validating or sending the JSON to a server

C# and Java represent heterogeneous unions as object/Object; Java nullability and optionality are comments because Java reference fields can be null and are not presence-tracked. Inference samples at most 300 array elements. Input is limited to 500 KB, 30,000 visited schema nodes and depth 24. No dependencies, upload, API or server processing.

functions: read HAR 1.2 or JSON captures from a local file or pasted text without uploading

show a compact chronological waterfall for up to 100 matching entries at once

Sensitive query values and URL credentials are masked in the request list, but hosts and URL paths can still identify private systems; users must inspect the original capture before sharing. Maximum input 5 MiB, 5,000 entries, 120,000 JSON values and depth 48; only 100 matching rows render per page. Response body contents and page-load time are not reconstructed; request durations may overlap, so their sum is not page-load time.

functions: paste robots.txt rules and enter a crawler product token plus up to 100 target URLs

Does not fetch robots.txt or URLs. Unsupported directives (including Crawl-delay and Sitemap) are reported but not applied. A robots.txt file is public crawler guidance, not access control, and does not guarantee crawling, indexing or ranking. Limits: 200 KB, 5,000 lines, 2,000 rules, 100 URLs, 4,096 characters per URL and a fixed total comparison-work budget.

functions: solve 2–20 integer congruences using exact BigInt arithmetic

inventory.boundary: Solves 2–20 integer congruences with moduli ≥2 and absolute input values ≤10¹². Uses exact local BigInt arithmetic. Compatible non-coprime systems are supported; incompatible systems are reported. It does not factor integers, prove primality or solve inequalities. Inputs stay in this browser.

functions: run configurable work and rest phases with an optional preparation countdown and up to 99 rounds

Settings and session data stay in the current page; no account, upload, API, storage or usage charge.

functions: generate a fresh locally randomized four-category matching puzzle at three difficulty settings

functions: edit Markdown with a focused writing surface, toolbar insertions, custom undo and redo, and a rendered preview

functions: convert Gregorian UTC date and time to Julian Date and Modified Julian Date

CSS percentages are relative to the element’s own dimensions and browsers may proportionally normalize overlapping corners. Values are limited to 500px or 100%; preview dimensions do not alter the emitted declaration.

functions: format GraphQL queries, mutations, subscriptions and SDL definitions with a real GraphQL parser

functions: estimate moonrise and moonset for a date, coordinates, and time zone

functions: turn person and manager rows into a hierarchy

functions: build a branching yes/no decision from editable question and outcome rows

functions: paste text and display one word at a time with adjustable words per minute
